title: Lotus
altText: A tall, narrow hanging scroll painted in ink on paper, showing lotus plants. The brushwork is expressive, and the format is much taller than it is wide.

source.verifiedBy: Art Institute of Chicago API record: title, artist (Qi Baishi, Chinese, 1861-1957), date, medium, credit line, classification (hanging scroll, painting), is_public_domain false and image dimensions (tall, narrow format) read from the record

context: Qi Baishi (1861 to 1957) was a Chinese painter who worked in the 20th century. This lotus painting is ink on paper mounted as a hanging scroll, a tall, narrow format that is displayed vertically and can be rolled up for storage.

descriptions.k: This is a tall, thin painting made with black ink. It shows lotus plants. A lotus is a water flower with big round leaves. Which parts look wet and soft? Which parts look sharp?
descriptions.g12: Qi Baishi was a painter from China. He painted lotus plants with ink on paper. The painting is very tall and narrow, and it hangs like a banner. Ink can be dark, light, wet, or dry. How many different kinds of ink strokes can you find?
descriptions.g35: Qi Baishi was a Chinese painter who lived from 1861 to 1957. This painting, called Lotus, is made with ink on paper and mounted as a hanging scroll, a tall, narrow shape you can roll up. Lotus is a water plant with large leaves and flowers. Look closely: how does the painter use light and dark ink to make plants with only one color?
descriptions.g68: Qi Baishi, who lived from 1861 to 1957, is among the best-known Chinese painters of the twentieth century. In Lotus, he uses ink on paper in a hanging scroll, a vertical format that suits tall plants. With just ink, a painter can vary dark and light tones, wet and dry strokes, and thick and thin lines. Notice how expressive brushwork can suggest leaves, stems, and flowers with confident, simple gestures.
descriptions.g910: Lotus is an ink painting on a hanging scroll by Qi Baishi (1861 to 1957), mounted in the tall, narrow format traditional to Chinese painting. Monochrome ink allows a wide range of tone and brush speed, from wet washes to dry, scratchy strokes. The vertical format emphasizes the growth of the plant. The lotus has long been a rich subject in East Asian art, and Qi's twentieth-century treatment combines tradition with a fresh, direct style.
descriptions.g1112: Qi Baishi (1861 to 1957) worked at a time when Chinese painters negotiated tradition and modern change. Lotus, an ink painting mounted as a hanging scroll, draws on a long East Asian tradition of painting plants, while its economy of means and direct brushwork reflect an individual modern voice. The lotus carries rich cultural associations, but the record offers no inscription or interpretation, so symbolic readings should be treated cautiously. The vertical scroll format shapes how viewers move their eyes and bodies in front of the work.

teacherNote.context: Qi Baishi (1861 to 1957) was a major twentieth-century Chinese painter. The museum record gives only basic data for this hanging scroll, so details such as inscriptions should be confirmed from the image.
directions: Have students paint a plant with one ink color and as many tones as possible, using water to lighten it.
Ask students to compare a tall vertical composition with a wide horizontal one of the same plant.
Discuss how a single flower can have different meanings in different cultures.
